cards.front: Recall a key point about Business Location and Expansion
cards.back: Location factors: proximity to customers/market, transport links, availability of suitable labour, cost of premises, competition, government incentives (grants, enterprise zones).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Business Location and Expansion
cards.back: Business plan: a document setting out the business idea, market research, financial forecasts, marketing strategy. Essential for securing finance from banks or investors. Shows the business has thought through its strategy.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Business Location and Expansion
cards.back: Organic growth: expanding from within - opening new outlets, increasing product range, growing online sales. Slow but controlled, less risky than external growth.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Business Location and Expansion
cards.back: External growth: mergers (two firms agree to join) and takeovers (one firm buys another). Faster growth but risky: cultural clash, high cost, integration problems. Franchising: rapid expansion with lower capital risk.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Business Location and Expansion
cards.back: Economies of scale: as a business grows, average cost per unit falls (bulk buying, technical efficiency, financial economies, marketing economies). Diseconomies of scale: beyond a certain size, average costs rise (poor communication, coordination problems, low morale).

cards.front: What should you know about business exam tips?
cards.back: For expansion questions: 1) Identify the growth method, 2) Explain how it works, 3) Give advantages and disadvantages, 4) Consider the business's specific circumstances (size, industry, resources), 5) Recommend the most appropriate method with justification.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Bigger is always better for a business because economies of scale mean lower costs. Correct: Economies of scale reduce average costs up to a point, but diseconomies of scale can set in when a business becomes too large: communication breaks down, decisions take longer, staff feel disconnected and morale falls, coordination costs increase.
